messages:
Alex: Quick question about /v1/generate semantics when stop sequences overlap with max_tokens. PR adds truncation on stop and we return logprobs up to the token before the stop — is that the intended contract for backward compatibility?

Maria: I thought we standardized on including the stop token in the text field (so users see the stop) but not in the logits/logprobs array. Is that what the spec says?

Raj: Historically clients relied on two things: 1) generated_text includes everything up to and including the stop string, 2) logprobs length matches the number of returned model tokens (so if stop is removed for logits, arrays are shorter). Changing that could break evals.

Jamie: For clarity, current implementation does: 
```
input: "Hello"
stop: ["\n\n"]
model returns tokens: ["Hello", "\n", "\n"]
response.text => "Hello\n\n"  # we concat tokens to text
response.logprobs => logprobs for ["Hello", "\n"]  # last stop token excluded from logprobs
```
This was chosen to avoid exposing internal special tokens from tokenizers.

Samir: Two followups: 1) max_tokens interaction. If max_tokens is hit in the middle of a stop pattern (e.g., stop is "END" and we only generated "EN" when max_tokens hit), do we treat that as a non-match and return partial text? 2) Temperature/top_p interplay: do we guarantee that temp=0 takes precedence over top_p? There have been subtle differences across runtimes.

Alex: Good points. My understanding: 
- Stop match requires full sequence match post-decoding, so partial prefix without full stop => no stop triggered. So you can get partial "EN" if max_tokens hits. That was the design to avoid ambiguous partial matches.
- For sampling: temp=0 is treated as deterministically greedy (ignores top_p). But we need to document that precisely — some runtimes do temp=0 + top_p<1 -> deterministic within top_p subset which is confusing for clients.

Maria: We should also be explicit about logprobs when max_tokens truncates mid-token (rare but possible with byte-level tokenization). We currently ensure logprobs align with token boundaries and never return a logprob for a token we didn't finish decoding. So truncated output will not have a logprob entry for the incomplete token.

Raj: This is important for downstream evals that compute per-token perplexity. If logprobs length != token_count used to produce text, folks will be confused. Can we add a compatibility mode flag like `include_partial_stop_logit=true`? That seems messy.

Jamie: I'd prefer we keep a single stable behavior and call it out in the API changelog. Back-compat wins. Proposed rule set: 
- Stop must fully match on decoded text.
- If stop matched, return text including stop, but omit logprobs for the final stop token.
- If max_tokens hit before stop, return partial text, and logprobs cover only complete tokens returned.
- temp=0 means greedy and top_p ignored (documented).

Samir: Sounds reasonable. I'll open a small RFC note and test harness. Also: edge case where stop is empty string or includes whitespace-only string — should be rejected at validation time.

Alex: Yes reject empty stop patterns. Also consider multiple stop sequences: if two stops overlap (e.g., "END" and "ND\n"), choose the earliest finishing match (i.e., smallest index after decoding).

Maria: Ping on PR review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/4123 — it implements the current behavior. Needs an explicit doc update and unit tests covering: partial stop w/ max_tokens, stop included in text but not logprobs, temp=0 + top_p interplay.

Raj: I'll take the tests for logprobs/perplexity. Jamie can add an integration test for overlap-of-stops. Samir can do a quick API doc patch.

Jamie: @Raj @Samir I left comments on the PR about tokenizer edge-cases. Also added a test matrix: 
- stop present before max_tokens 
- stop broken by max_tokens 
- overlapping stop candidates 
- extreme temps (0, 1.2) with top_p combos

Samir: FYI deploy-bot ran canary today on staging and reported no regressions:
deploy-bot: [canary] service/serve succeeded in staging (canary id c-2026-03-14). No errors in 1h window. :white_check_mark:

Alex: Awesome. Plan: land PR once tests added, then update /docs/api/generation.md with explicit contract bullets and examples. Also add a short note in changelog for Dedicated customers (they rely on strict behavior).

Maria: One more operational note — we need to make sure older SDKs that expect `generated_text` top-level field still get it for a deprecation window. The PR currently writes both `choices[].text` and legacy `generated_text` for 30 days behind a deprecation header. Agree?

Raj: Agree. Add tests for both response shapes.

Alex: OK. Action items: 
- Samir: docs + validation for empty stop (ETA EOD)
- Raj: logprob/perplexity tests (ETA tomorrow)
- Jamie: integration overlap tests and PR review (ETA today)
- Maria: SDK compatibility note + changelog blurb (ETA EOD)

Samir: I'll also add an example in the docs showing the recommended way to handle logprobs when stop tokens are omitted from logprobs (example code snippet).

Alex: Thanks everyone — I'll merge once the test matrix is green. :rocket:
